citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
When inspecting the wool-sheep at the end of the trail that is open to the public, inspectors observed a dead wool-sheep
(eartag #0164) behind one of the concrete shelters. The representative that does daily animal checks said he had not
seen this dead animal. The sheep's decomposing condition suggests it had died more than 24 hours before inspectors
found it. Inadequate daily observations does not assure that an animal that is sick or injured is observed and timely
reported to the AV for appropriate care. Ensure that a routine of adequate daily observations is in place so that timely and
accurate information on problems of animal health, behavior, and well-being is conveyed to the attending veterinarian.
***Correct from June 5, 2026 forward.

Inspectors observed areas in some enclosures that were not maintained in good repair and could cause injury to animals:
-The inside area of the alpaca shelter has rusted sharp edges that alpacas could touch.
-Two areas by the alpacas' water tank have partially buried wire/fencing sticking up from the ground that alpacas could
injure their feet/legs on.
-The shelter area with the black Hawaiian sheep has a broken panel with a disconnected pipe that has edges sheep can
touch.
-A gatepost in front of the black Hawaiian sheep shelter has wire points sheep can touch.
-Concrete shade shelters in the wooled-sheep pasture have re-bar points sticking out that have sharp edges.
Sharp rusted edges, loose wire, edges on a gate, wire points, and re-bar points could all cause injury to animals. The
facility must maintain primary enclosures in a manner that protects animals from injury.
***Correct by 6/8/2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
Additional Inspectors:
Scott Welch, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
